newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate passes budget bill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate passes budget bill.

text.p: The Australian Senate on Wednesday passed the last major budget bill with only minor amendments.

A spokesman for Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman estimated that the government had secured savings of A$350 million over four years, compared with the A$400 million it originally sought and the A$150 million that the Senate was prepared to accept last year.
"We are very happy with that outcome," the spokesman said.
The bill sought to implement part of the government's August budget, which included savings that would rise to A$7.2 billion next fiscal year, from July.
The government wanted to exclude immigrants from most social security for two years after arrival.

It argued that this was the usual policy in other countries but left-leaning minor parties in the Senate, backed by two independents, heavily amended the bill in December, negating most of its fiscal effect.
The government then sent the bill back to the Senate, demanding that the upper house think again. This time the independents generally sided with the government.
